nodes.description: The brain in HFM is deprived of folate by two routes at once: low blood folate limits delivery across the blood-brain barrier, and absent choroid plexus transport leaves CSF folate near zero, starving periventricular brain that depends on diffusion from CSF. This is why neurological disease in HFM appears earlier than in FOLR1-related cerebral folate deficiency and can progress even after the anemia is corrected.

nodes.description: The choroid plexus normally transports folate uphill into the CSF, keeping CSF folate two to three times higher than blood. PCFT is required for this transport together with folate receptor alpha; in cell models PCFT exports folate from acidified endosomes after FRalpha-mediated endocytosis, which would explain why loss of either protein blocks the pathway at the neutral pH of the choroid plexus. In HFM CSF folate stays extremely low even after blood folate is normalized with parenteral folate.

nodes.description: Disease-specific therapy is high-dose 5-formyltetrahydrofolate (folinic acid, leucovorin), preferably intramuscular and ideally the active isomer (levoleucovorin, levofolinic acid), started as early as possible and titrated to bring CSF folate trough concentrations as close as possible to the age-specific normal range. Small doses correct the anemia, immune defect and gastrointestinal signs; much higher doses are needed for adequate CSF folate, and in a direct comparison only intramuscular (not oral) dosing normalized it. Folic acid should be avoided, because it binds folate receptor alpha very tightly and may impair physiological folate transport across the choroid plexus. Early treatment can allow normal development: one woman treated from two months of age was normal into adulthood and completed higher education. Affected women should be on their full folinic acid regimen well before conception; infants of mothers with HFM have not shown an increased risk of neural tube defects.

nodes.description: Biallelic SLC46A1 variants abolish or severely impair the proton-coupled folate transporter, an electrogenic folate:proton symporter that is the major route of folate uptake at low pH. Most variants cause loss of PCFT protein through frameshifts, premature stop codons or aberrant splicing; in-frame missense variants either destabilize the protein (G147R, D156Y, A335D, G338R) or are expressed but transport-defective (R113C/S, P425R).
